slides.title: High Fidelity Capture, Reconstruction, and Transfer of Human Demonstrations for Robot-Assisted Bathing
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for capturing and transferring contact-rich human bathing demonstrations to a soft robotic hand, contributing to the development of safe physical human-robot interaction for RwB.

card.one_liner: A framework for capturing and transferring high-fidelity human bathing demonstrations to a robot-assisted system.
card.key_idea: Uses contact regions as a processing primitive to reconstruct synchronized motion, shape, and force, then retargets these to a soft robotic hand and arm.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a dataset of 128 captures (3 clinicians, 6 subjects) and real-world deployment on a mannequin using open- and closed-loop control.
card.limitation: Significant sim-to-real gap; closed-loop control uses aggregate pressure sums rather than distributions; not yet ready for human subjects.

slides.title: Detection and Ranging of Transient Extrinsic Contacts Based on 6D Dynamic Tactile Sensing
slides.tldr: FAST EXTRINSIC CONTACT DETECTION AND RANGING
slides.highlight: This work introduces TECDAR for rapid, millimeter-level localization of extrinsic contacts, supporting the physics-based skill estimation and delicate manipulation goals of MOSAIC.

card.one_liner: TECDAR enables fast, millimeter-level extrinsic contact localization on grasped objects using a single 6D IMU sensor.
card.key_idea: An event-driven framework using an accelerometer to trigger contact detection and an Extended Kalman Filter to map gyroscopic angular velocity to contact coordinates via differential kinematics.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on line and point-contact tasks (e.g., books, pens) achieving ~7mm average accuracy and 20ms control response cycles.
card.limitation: Higher localization error (5.36mm) compared to high-resolution visuotactile sensors, which offer sub-millimeter precision.

slides.title: AdaDexGrasp: Adaptive Dexterous Grasping via 3D Visuo-Tactile Representation Fusion
slides.tldr: ADAPTIVE DEXTEROUS GRASPING VIA VISUO-TACTILE FUSION
slides.highlight: This framework integrates 3D visual perception and tactile feedback to enable contact-aware grasp generation and dynamic refinement, improving success rates across diverse objects.

card.one_liner: AdaDexGrasp improves dexterous grasping by fusing 3D geometry with finger-specific tactile feedback for adaptive refinement.
card.key_idea: A framework using a contact-aware representation that binds tactile signals to finger identities, enabling initial grasp generation, stability classification, and iterative pose adaptation via a diffusion-based model.
card.evaluation: Evaluated in IsaacGym and real-world (Psibot hand) on seen/unseen objects. Outperformed 10 baselines, achieving 83% success on unseen categories in simulation.
card.limitation: Denser tactile modalities (e.g., shear forces) were avoided as they increased data requirements and widened the sim-to-real gap.

slides.title: Trajectory Divergence Horizon Decision for Reliable Dual-Arm Surgical Subtask Manipulation
slides.tldr: ADAPTIVE EXECUTION HORIZON FOR SURGICAL VLA MODELS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a test-time mechanism to improve the reliability of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models in surgical robotics by adaptively truncating action sequences based on trajectory divergence.

card.one_liner: TDHD improves dual-arm surgical VLA reliability by adaptively truncating open-loop action sequences based on trajectory divergence.
card.key_idea: A test-time mechanism measuring L2 distance between two flow-matching trajectories generated with small noise perturbations to trigger replanning via absolute and ratio thresholds.
card.evaluation: Tested on a da Vinci-like robot with 600 demonstrations. Success rates rose from 55% to 60% (needle) and 55% to 80% (tissue).
card.limitation: Evaluations were limited to controlled phantom environments and a small set of subtasks, lacking diverse anatomical variety.

slides.title: VIDP: Variable Impedance Diffusion Policy for Compliant Robot Manipulation from Diverse Demonstrations
slides.tldr: VARIABLE IMPEDANCE DIFFUSION POLICY FOR COMPLIANT MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This framework enables robots to learn variable impedance control from kinematic demonstrations without force sensors, improving success rates in contact-rich tasks.

card.one_liner: VIDP learns variable impedance control from kinematic demonstrations to enable compliant, contact-rich robot manipulation.
card.key_idea: Uses a Task-Parameterized Directionality-Aware Mixture Model (TP-DAMM) to extract stiffness profiles from trajectory variances, which a Diffusion Policy then predicts alongside pose actions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on peg-in-hole, pulley assembly, and cable routing tasks; outperformed fixed-impedance baselines in success rates and reduced interaction forces.
card.limitation: The provided text does not clearly state a specific limitation or risk when using the framework.

slides.title: SpaceVLA: Spatially Grounded VLA for Robotic Manipulation with User-Authored Grasp and Place Anchors
slides.tldr: SPATIALLY GROUNDED VLA FOR ROBOTIC MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces Visual Intent Anchors to provide explicit spatial intent for VLA models via image-space overlays, achieving high grasp success rates in pick-and-place tasks.

card.one_liner: SpaceVLA uses user-defined visual anchors to provide explicit spatial intent for robotic pick-and-place tasks.
card.key_idea: Fine-tuned OpenVLA-7B with LoRA to predict 7-DoF actions using RGB observations overlaid with color-coded image-space masks representing user-specified grasp and placement targets.
card.evaluation: Evaluated in Unity on 80 held-out episodes; achieved 91.25% success rate, significantly outperforming no-anchor (50%) and random-anchor (77.5%) baselines.
card.limitation: Anchors are fixed image-space masks under a static camera, failing to track objects or maintain alignment during viewpoint changes.

slides.title: C2Dex: Contact-Consistent Reconstruction and Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Monocular Video
slides.highlight: C2Dex improves the transfer of human manipulation behaviors from monocular video to dexterous robots by using stable object-side contacts to ensure physical plausibility and geometric consistency.

card.one_liner: C2Dex converts monocular human videos into executable dexterous robot trajectories using stable object-side contact representations.
card.key_idea: Aggregates noisy frame-wise observations into stable canonical object-space contacts to guide HOI reconstruction and preserve local interaction geometry via Laplacian optimization and residual RL.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on DexYCB and TACO datasets; achieved trajectory success rates of 57.78% and 26.67%, respectively, outperforming baselines. Validated via real-robot replay.
card.limitation: Struggles with severe occlusions, extreme viewpoints, pose drift in object estimation, and complex in-hand manipulation like finger gaiting.

slides.title: Embodied Multimodal Grounding for Open-Vocabulary Mobile Manipulation via Semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting
slides.tldr: EMBODIED MULTIMODAL GROUNDING FOR MOBILE MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This work presents a multimodal grounding framework using Semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting to improve robustness under clutter and occlusion, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and scene reasoning.

card.one_liner: A multimodal grounding framework using Semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting to improve open-vocabulary mobile manipulation robustness.
card.key_idea: Integrates active multi-view Semantic-3DGS for 3D localization and obstacle reasoning, reachability-aware base positioning, and a diffusion-based VLA policy with late-block semantic injection.
card.evaluation: Real-robot trials (up to 50) against PointVLA and DexVLA; showed 60% long-horizon and 74% cluttered-scene success rates.
card.limitation: Targets quasi-static manipulation; requires off-board GPU and does not support fast dynamic interaction or zero-shot skill acquisition.
